purpose: Test whether Zipf + information-weighted norms predict observed power-law eigenspectrum

greedy_packing.description: Sort contributions by f_i * ||v_i||^2, pack contiguous blocks into eigenvalues
greedy_packing.note: Assumes perfect directional alignment (unrealistic upper bound)

monte_carlo_info_weighted.description: Random unit directions scaled by sqrt(-log(P(token))), n=49152-151936, 1000 trials
monte_carlo_info_weighted.note: Norm weighting alone produces FLAT spectra (MP-like)

monte_carlo_uniform.description: Random unit directions, uniform norms (Marchenko-Pastur baseline)

directional_organization_alpha.interpretation: Fraction of theoretical maximum directional structure; decreases with d

conclusions: Norm weighting alone does NOT produce power-law spectra (random directions → flat)
Power law requires DIRECTIONAL STRUCTURE created by training
Degree of directional organization is d-dependent (alpha decreasing with d)
Effective Zipf exponent of training data is ~0.5, not 1.0
Partial organization (alpha~0.3-0.5) is the operating regime of real models
